text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former President Turgut Ozal to be commemorated on the first anniversary of his death on Thursday.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz predicts the Islamist-led government will break up after the week-long Feast of Sacrifice holiday.
- President Suleyman Demirel in a row with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller over the appointment of a new national police chief force.
- Government printed 180 billion lira in order to pay salaries of civil servants and pensioners who were given a pay rise before the holiday.
- Head of the secularist army visited Ciller and Demirel on Wednesday after Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan left Turkey for the Moslem Haj pilgrimage.
- Islamist foundations, Koran teaching centers and religious associations breach the law by collecting the skins of sacrificed sheep in the Eid al-Adha holiday for revenue raising.
- A large number of touristic sites are up for sale in structural reform of crucial industry.
- The number of traffic accidents has decreased by 40 percent compared to past years since a traffic came into force.
